newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: RTRS-Sacked army chief says PNG's Chan must quit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Sacked army chief says PNG's Chan must quit.

text.p: Papua New Guinea's sacked army commander demanded on Friday that Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan quit in the coming days, rejecting a conciliatory gesture from Chan over a controversial mercenary contract.
"I cannot back down on the call for this prime minister and the ministers who are implicated to resign from their ministerial offices," Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok told reporters.
Singirok sparked PNG's crisis on Monday by demanding that Chan and two other ministers resign for having hired mercenaries to put down a long-running rebellion on Bougainville island.
Singirok was promptly sacked and has since become the focal point for violent anti-government dissent. He has consistently urged soldiers not to join in the civil unrest.
Singirok told a news conference at Port Moresby's Murray barracks that his original demand for the mercenaries to leave the country was now being met.
But he rejected an inquiry, announced by Chan on Thursday, into the US$36 million mercenary contract because he said Chan himself would control it.
